rationale: The previous candidate with base_speed 0.9, kp 5, kd 1.5, and ki 1.5 showed improved stability and reduced steering oscillation on oval and s-bend tracks but still failed to complete the slalom track, going off track early with high steering oscillation and rms error. The slalom track demands even more precise control and stability. The feedback suggests further reducing base_speed if slalom completion still fails, and softening PID gains if steering oscillation remains high. The race data confirms these issues persist. Therefore, I reduce base_speed further to 0.8 to lower speed and improve control in tight curves. I also reduce kp to 4 and kd to 1 to soften the steering response and reduce oscillations. I increase ki to 2.0 to enhance steady-state error correction, aiming to lower rms error on curves. The geometry and sensor layout remain unchanged as they are stable and well balanced. The line loss strategy remains 'last_direction' to maintain effective recovery. I continue to request the full set of observations to monitor completion, progress, errors, line loss, and control metrics. I expect these changes to improve slalom completion by prioritizing stability and precision over speed, reducing overshoot and steering oscillations, and improving line tracking accuracy.
